svg.font-family: 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next', 'Segoe UI', 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Tiers of domains
svg.desc: Tiers of domains. Each tier is a repository of its own, with its own curator and releases. The top domain, domains/federation, is where this build starts, and may itself be a member of another domain. It names domains/domain1 and domains/domain2, which are tier 1. Each names a domain in turn, domains/domain3 and domains/domain4, which are tier 2. Those name the bundles, tier 3: any number under each, one repository each, drawn as a stack, and one shared model, an upper ontology such as gist, named by both at one release, so that it joins the workspace once. Each box gives a domain concept's path and an example namespace, such as https://w3id.org/<org>/domain1/knowledge/. Four rules keep a tree of domains sound. One: every domain bounds a workspace of its own, and a build knows nothing of a domain above its top domain. Two: confirming a domain confirms the delegation, that the domain belongs and who answers for it, not what its members say. Three, the diamond rule: two domains may name the same bundle; at the same release it joins the workspace once, and at different releases the build stops until the two owners agree on one release and both pin it. Four: the depth is the top domain's to set; max_depth is how many tiers the build follows, 3 unless set, a domain at the last tier stops the build, and a domain may not name itself or a domain above it. Namespaces may not nest: give a domain a namespace beside its members', never above them.
